perspective:
Ethan’s available information:

- Ethan knows Gary is his long-time friend from middle school and a doctor. Ethan himself is a plumber.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep.
- Concerned, Ethan invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat, telling him his health mattered and he hated seeing him like this.
- Gary told Ethan he appreciated the concern but couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more going on than professional obligations.
- Ethan told Gary they had been friends since middle school and Gary could tell him anything; Ethan was there to help, not judge.
- Gary told Ethan it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden him with his problems.
- Gary later opened up to Ethan about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges.
- Ethan offered to help prioritize tasks and delegate responsibilities. Gary agreed he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed progress and challenges, saw Gary making efforts, and felt hopeful and proud. Ethan told Gary he was proud and available whenever Gary needed to talk.
- Gary told Ethan things were better, he was less overwhelmed, and he had time for a movie.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing a healthier work-life balance and capable of handling things on his own. Ethan felt satisfied and happy for him.
- Ethan told Gary he was always just a call away but knew Gary had it, then stepped back.
- Gary thanked Ethan, said he couldn’t have done it without his support, and felt more in control.
